paragraphs: "Seer, huh?
Yes, you can compare me to that child in some regard."
Nux chuckled, and Zala just stared at him in utter awe.
Once again, Nux used his ability to amplify the feeling of awe he felt to an absurd degree. It was almost pushed to the degree of fanaticism.
Yes, he couldn’t manipulate their memories, but emotions? He could do whatever he wanted with those.
"Anyways, are you prepared to reform your Law?"
"I-I am."
Zala nodded.

Nux nodded back as he then placed his hand over Zala’s head. A few patterns appeared all over Nux’s body as he read Zala’s memories using his ability. Zala didn’t resist; he just stared at the being in front of him with absolute awe.
Once he was done, Nux devoured his cultivation, turning him from a Primordial to a mortal. Then, he raised his cultivation to the Saint Stage and,
"Reform your Law."
He ordered, already knowing what Law Zala was going to form.
It wasn’t very different from the Law he had before; it was just a stronger version, and Nux preferred it that way.
After all, the reason he ’chose’ him was because of his Law.
Law of Eternal Mark Read new chapters at freewebnovel
A law that allowed him to place a barely noticeable and ever-present mark on any person or object.
Yes, it was a simple marking ability, nothing that would usually catch someone’s eye, but for someone like Nux, it was different.
If he had this power, he could easily track beings from anywhere he wanted, and with his Space Laws, appear right next to them no matter where they were.
Yes, he had Aeliana’s way to mark and track a being as well, but...
A perceptive being could sense his energy if he used Aeliana’s method. A being with a higher quality of energy could even remove that energy.
It was nothing more than a party trick that was easy to counter if the person knew they were marked.
But with the Law of Eternal Mark, it was different.
Even if the target knew they were marked, which in itself was difficult since the mark was barely noticeable, it was extremely difficult to get rid of it.
And what’s even better?
This was just the start.
After all, Zala wasn’t the only one who had comprehended this Law.
Nux had comprehended it as well, and he had added his own understanding to it.
"Reform your Law."
BOOOM
BOOOOOOOOM
Their auras exploded. The energy of this Law formed above the two of them, then, the energy was combined and rushed into Zala’s body.
And the change happened.
The Law of Eternal Mark turned into the Law of Absolute Mark.
A Law that allowed a being to place an imperceptible, indestructible, omnipresent mark on anything—be it a person, object, or even a concept.
Yes, imperceptible, indestructible, and omnipresent. It was a mark that couldn’t be sensed, destroyed, or removed.
Yes, Transcendents with specific Laws could somehow suppress it, but even they couldn’t completely remove it.
And that wasn’t it. Since Nux had added some of his own comprehension to the Law as well, he had also added another power to teleport next to the marked entity.
Of course, since Zala hadn’t comprehended the Space Law, the energy he would need to use would be absurd,
But it was still a strong ability.
Zala couldn’t believe it.
"A-An Absolute..."
He knew what this meant.
To think he would be able to form an Absolute Law...
No, he didn’t form it.
Zala wasn’t arrogant enough to believe he could form an Absolute Law, even if he was given a second chance. It was something different.
He was... given this law.
By this being...
By the Ruler.
To think this being not only allowed him to reform his Law but even managed to strengthen it.
All the doubts he had about all of this being a lie disappeared in an instant. He collapsed on his knees and,
"Lord Ruler, I swear to always remain loyal to you."
He swore his loyalty, overwhelmed by the excessive emotions he was feeling.
"Continue cultivating, understand your new Law, and breakthrough. I will not be aiding you anymore."
"I understand! I am greatly honored by your help!"
Zala nodded, and then, with a wave of Nux’s hand, he was teleported away to a Star where he could break through to the Primordial Stage.
Once Zala was gone, Felberta and the others appeared next to Nux, and unable to hold herself back, Vyriana questioned,
"How strong?"
"Level 174."
"Just one?"
The Dragon frowned.
"Well, this is just the beginning."
Nux smiled as his eyes fell on Shadow, who was talking to yet another ’black soul.’
"The Ruler will rise to the top again, and in his journey, he will need new entities to watch over the Universe.
You are chosen as one of the contenders.
Are you willing..."
"She seems to be having fun."
Felberta chuckled.
"She’s a natural."
Nux laughed as well.
"I didn’t think Shadow, of all people, would be good at fooling people."
Felberta stared as she then turned towards Lane and,
"I wonder where she got it from."
"The two of us are independent entities."
Lane quickly defended herself, wanting to have nothing to do with shameless Shadow.
"Right..."
Felberta, however, just nodded with a light smile on her face, not believing her sister at all.
Time passed. One by one, Shadow continued to fool the ’chosen black souls’ and sent them Nux’s way. Nux helped them reform their Law and turned them all into Divines.
And as the Universe, as he did something he was supposed to do and accepted their Laws, he continued to get stronger and stronger.
And after advancing the last of the 18 entities,
BOOOM
His aura burst out and,
"Level 178."
He commented.
And silence fell over.
It was still too slow.
"It’s okay, we just need to devour 20 more."
Vyriana nodded.
"Let’s take 30 to be on the safe side."
Felberta nodded.
Nux, on the other hand, just shrugged.
For now, his attention was on someone else.
"Ember is back with a mission."
Yes, it was time the Leander Family continued taking more missions and participated in the War.

chapters.title: Chapter 1912: Don’t be foolish, Nux Leander.
paragraphs: "That was quick, I thought it would take a while."
Felberta commented with a surprised look on her face.
"We thought the same."
Astaria nodded.

Usually, when a Mercenary Party goes on a break, many other parties replace them, and it affects their fame. So the number of missions they can accept falls, and it takes them more than a few days to find a mission they could take.

The Leander Family was expecting the same. However, the instant they walked into the Mercenary Hall, the mercenaries inside froze. There was almost no one there who didn’t recognize them, and before the women could even react,
The staff sitting at the counter rushed towards them and welcomed them with a straight bow and a face that screamed desperation.

"But it looks like in our absence, the number of missions that came specifically for our party continued to rise and piled up. Even when the Mercenary Halls mentioned that we were on a break, it didn’t do anything.

The people wanted to wait for our return rather than hand over the mission to another party. Because of that, the number of piled-up missions in the Mercenary Hall is alarmingly high, and they were waiting for our return to complete all those missions."
Ember explained the situation.
"That’s... overwhelming."
Felberta commented.
"Indeed."
The Goddess of War nodded.

"The instant we got there, they handed us over a hundred missions, all of which specifically requested our aid, so no one else could take them. They told us to take as long as we want to complete all these missions."
"All of them?"
Felberta raised her eyebrow.
"This is just one of the Mercenary Halls. There are about a hundred more where we have made appearances. The situation there should be somewhat similar."
"So about a thousand missions piled up in 10 years?"
"Well, some of the missions would be repeated, and it also depends on how often we went to those Mercenary Halls.
But there should be about 300 missions."
Ember answered.
"Of course, this is a rough estimate, could be more or less."
Felberta nodded in understanding.
"300 missions aren’t a lot, are they?"
Evane questioned with a frown.
"All these missions are related to wars. See it as 300 worlds waiting for us to save them."
Ember clarified, and Evane’s expression changed.
"It’s funny how hundreds of worlds see us as some group of messiahs while our husband goes around destroying the worlds like some evil fiend.
It is hard to tell whether we are the good of this Universe or the evil."
Aisha chuckled as she stared at Nux.
"We aren’t anything of this Universe.
We are not a part of it."
Vyriana answered.
The women shrugged as well.
"Alright, enough talking.
Let’s start completing the missions."
Astaria spoke as she stared at the women. Everyone nodded, and the Leander Family returned to the world of mercenaries.

One by one, they completed all the missions with perfection. Since most of the missions they took came from Low-Level Worlds, the strongest enemies they had to face were the Primordials, and even that was rare since that was the responsibility of the world leaders.
Under Ember’s command, they simply needed to take part in the battle as a part of the army and annihilate the enemy while protecting their own, and they did this splendidly.
Of course, there were times when the Primordials tried to attack them, but Nux, who was in their shadow, protected them, and Aeliana came to help as well.
The rate at which the missions were completed was surprising. Of course, this was when the women weren’t even focusing on completing the missions.
After all, their major focus was never to complete the mission.
It was to gather information.
Information about the worlds that Nux could devour, and Nux didn’t hold back either.
He continued to devour different worlds, and every single time, the Universe reacted to his actions in anger.
It had honestly become a game, and Nux was worried that the Universe might rage quit.

The number of ’slots’ he had continued to rise. However, he didn’t devour more beings. His conditions were harsh. He wanted their Law or abilities to be somewhat related to the Primordial Energies or be something unique that he could use.
He didn’t wish to devour just anyone just so he could break through to the Primordial Stage.
Of course, this didn’t mean he wasn’t going to break through at all. If push comes to shove and he couldn’t find beings with interesting Laws or abilities, he would devour anyone and break through.
He was being patient.
5 years, that is all that he was giving himself. If he couldn’t find anyone in these five years, he would break through to the Primordial Stage through force.
Time passed. The women continued to complete the missions. Everything went smoothly.
Too smoothly, in fact.
It was almost as if something was wrong.
For the last 30 missions, the women were never once attacked by the Primordials. It was as if the Primordials were scared of attacking them.
No, it wasn’t just the Primordials. It seemed like the enemy world itself was scared when they found out that the Leander Family was with the enemies.
And it made sense.

Their party’s fame was rising at an absurd pace. Almost every Low-Level World that belonged to the two factions at war with each other knew of them. They knew of their record, and they knew what it meant if they were on their or the opposite side.
Continue your journey on freewebnovel
It had reached the point where sometimes, they received missions from two opposing worlds and had to choose one of them.
Because of this, the rewards they were receiving continued to rise further and further.
Right now, the Leander Family was the most highly sought party, and the rewards they received were higher than any party of Sovereigns throughout the Universe.
What’s even stranger?
The reward continued to increase and increase even further.
Of course, the women didn’t complain. With the rewards, their connections were increasing as well. More than a few Middle-Level Worlds had offered to take them in.
Honestly, with how much attention they were receiving, the women knew it was time for them to go on a break again.
After all, the last thing they wanted was to attract the attention of a High-Level, or worse, a Supreme-Level World.
The women decided that after one last mission, they would retreat.
For this, they chose a relatively easier mission.
The mission was similar to others—two low-level worlds, both having a high number of Sovereigns but only one Primordial Leader.
With Ember in charge, the Sovereigns on their side very quickly overpowered the enemy, but then,
Something happened.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM
An extremely horrifying aura burst out, crushing everyone present on the battlefield, including the two Primordials, to their knees.
Yes, every being on the battlefield was neutralized.
And finally, a 2-meter-tall being, whose body seemed to be made of black, foamy material covered with endless malice, descended onto the world.
His facial features weren’t very clear; it was as if no one here was worthy of seeing his face.
"I finally caught you, you ra—"
The being spoke, his voice slow, heavy, and dreadful.
But then,
He froze.
The women he was here for...
They weren’t here.
"Where did they go!?"
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM
He screamed, releasing an aura so horrifying that—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The world shook, instantly revealing its core as a form of submission.
What else could it do?
How could it, a low-level world, face a Transcendent?
Of course, the being didn’t come here for a mere low-level world. With a wave of his hand, the Primordial who had hired the Leander Family rose into the air and appeared next to him, trembling.
"Where are they?"
The being questioned, his voice so menacing that the Primordial Leader could see his world shaking.
"I-I don’t know...
T-They were just h-her—"
"Just here!? Then where did they go!? Did they just disappear into the air!?"
"T-They m-must have teleported awa—"
"I released my aura before I came here. They shouldn’t be able to move."
"A-Aura doesn’t seem to w-work on th—"
"Are you comparing your meager aura with mine?"
The being’s voice became even heavier.

Of course, he had also heard that aura didn’t work on those women, and since he couldn’t take any chances—because of how many times he had failed before—he wasn’t just relying on his aura. He had also sealed away any form of spatial movement from this world.
No being could teleport away from here.
Unless, of course, that being had the complete Law of Absolute Space, and meager artifacts that simply messed with the flow of Space Laws wouldn’t work on him.
Yes, the instant Nux sensed the Transcendent’s descent, he teleported his wives away.
Yes, his wives, not him.
This man had targeted his wives—how could he let him go?
With a demonic grin on his face, he teleported both the Primordial and the Transcendent to the execution ground, an empty space surrounded by thousands of asteroids.
"W-What?"
The Primordial stuttered.
The Transcendent, on the other hand, narrowed his eyes.
"Who is it?"
He called out.
A being capable of teleporting him away without him being able to resist—especially when teleportation shouldn’t have been possible—he could tell that this being was anything but simple.
He wanted to talk it out and clear whatever misunderstanding they might have had, but—
"I’ll be the one asking."
Nux’s voice echoed throughout the surroundings, and suddenly, the space stretched endlessly. The Laws of Space were altered, making it impossible for both the Transcendent and the Primordial to move.
’I guess I need to break through in order to deal with this one, huh?’
Nux thought in his head, but just as he considered breaking through, he paused as another idea popped into his mind.
’Can a Sovereign defeat a Transcendent?’
With a wave of his hand, he teleported next to the slave he had given the relic to.
"Give me the sword."
He ordered, and under the effect of the Slave Seal, the slave quickly passed the relic without any questions.
Nux teleported back. It all happened in less than a few seconds. It was more than enough time for a Transcendent-level being to do something, but right now, even a Transcendent was helpless.
Nux quickly made the connection with the relic,
Or at least, that was what he tried to do.
But before he could—
Time around him slowed down.
Even the Transcendent’s attacks, which were coming toward Nux, slowed to an absurd speed, surprising even Nux.
Then suddenly, he heard a voice. A voice so sweet and lovely that he couldn’t believe his ears.
"Don’t be foolish, Nux Leander."

sentences.text: "That was quick, I thought it would take a while."
Felberta commented with a surprised look on her face.
"We thought the same."
Astaria nodded.
Usually, when a Mercenary Party goes on a break, many other parties replace them, and it affects their fame.
So the number of missions they can accept falls, and it takes them more than a few days to find a mission they could take.
The Leander Family was expecting the same.
However, the instant they walked into the Mercenary Hall, the mercenaries inside froze.
There was almost no one there who didn’t recognize them, and before the women could even react,
The staff sitting at the counter rushed towards them and welcomed them with a straight bow and a face that screamed desperation.
"But it looks like in our absence, the number of missions that came specifically for our party continued to rise and piled up.
Even when the Mercenary Halls mentioned that we were on a break, it didn’t do anything.
The people wanted to wait for our return rather than hand over the mission to another party.
Because of that, the number of piled-up missions in the Mercenary Hall is alarmingly high, and they were waiting for our return to complete all those missions."
Ember explained the situation.
"That’s... overwhelming."
Felberta commented.
"Indeed."
The Goddess of War nodded.
"The instant we got there, they handed us over a hundred missions, all of which specifically requested our aid, so no one else could take them.
They told us to take as long as we want to complete all these missions."
"All of them?"
Felberta raised her eyebrow.
"This is just one of the Mercenary Halls.
There are about a hundred more where we have made appearances.
The situation there should be somewhat similar."
"So about a thousand missions piled up in 10 years?"
"Well, some of the missions would be repeated, and it also depends on how often we went to those Mercenary Halls.
But there should be about 300 missions."
Ember answered.
"Of course, this is a rough estimate, could be more or less."
Felberta nodded in understanding.
"300 missions aren’t a lot, are they?"
Evane questioned with a frown.
"All these missions are related to wars.
See it as 300 worlds waiting for us to save them."
Ember clarified, and Evane’s expression changed.
"It’s funny how hundreds of worlds see us as some group of messiahs while our husband goes around destroying the worlds like some evil fiend.
It is hard to tell whether we are the good of this Universe or the evil."
Aisha chuckled as she stared at Nux.
"We aren’t anything of this Universe.
We are not a part of it."
Vyriana answered.
The women shrugged as well.
"Alright, enough talking.
Let’s start completing the missions."
Astaria spoke as she stared at the women.
Everyone nodded, and the Leander Family returned to the world of mercenaries.
One by one, they completed all the missions with perfection.

Since most of the missions they took came from Low-Level Worlds, the strongest enemies they had to face were the Primordials, and even that was rare since that was the responsibility of the world leaders.
Under Ember’s command, they simply needed to take part in the battle as a part of the army and annihilate the enemy while protecting their own, and they did this splendidly.
Of course, there were times when the Primordials tried to attack them, but Nux, who was in their shadow, protected them, and Aeliana came to help as well.
The rate at which the missions were completed was surprising.
Of course, this was when the women weren’t even focusing on completing the missions.
After all, their major focus was never to complete the mission.
It was to gather information.
Information about the worlds that Nux could devour, and Nux didn’t hold back either.
He continued to devour different worlds, and every single time, the Universe reacted to his actions in anger.
It had honestly become a game, and Nux was worried that the Universe might rage quit.
The number of ’slots’ he had continued to rise.
However, he didn’t devour more beings.
His conditions were harsh.
He wanted their Law or abilities to be somewhat related to the Primordial Energies or be something unique that he could use.
He didn’t wish to devour just anyone just so he could break through to the Primordial Stage.
Of course, this didn’t mean he wasn’t going to break through at all.
If push comes to shove and he couldn’t find beings with interesting Laws or abilities, he would devour anyone and break through.
He was being patient.
5 years, that is all that he was giving himself.
If he couldn’t find anyone in these five years, he would break through to the Primordial Stage through force.
Time passed.
The women continued to complete the missions.
Everything went smoothly.
Too smoothly, in fact.
It was almost as if something was wrong.
For the last 30 missions, the women were never once attacked by the Primordials.
It was as if the Primordials were scared of attacking them.
No, it wasn’t just the Primordials.
It seemed like the enemy world itself was scared when they found out that the Leander Family was with the enemies.
And it made sense.
Their party’s fame was rising at an absurd pace.
Almost every Low-Level World that belonged to the two factions at war with each other knew of them.
They knew of their record, and they knew what it meant if they were on their or the opposite side.
Continue your journey on freewebnovel
It had reached the point where sometimes, they received missions from two opposing worlds and had to choose one of them.
Because of this, the rewards they were receiving continued to rise further and further.
Right now, the Leander Family was the most highly sought party, and the rewards they received were higher than any party of Sovereigns throughout the Universe.
What’s even stranger?
The reward continued to increase and increase even further.
Of course, the women didn’t complain.
With the rewards, their connections were increasing as well.
More than a few Middle-Level Worlds had offered to take them in.
Honestly, with how much attention they were receiving, the women knew it was time for them to go on a break again.
After all, the last thing they wanted was to attract the attention of a High-Level, or worse, a Supreme-Level World.
The women decided that after one last mission, they would retreat.
For this, they chose a relatively easier mission.
The mission was similar to others—two low-level worlds, both having a high number of Sovereigns but only one Primordial Leader.
With Ember in charge, the Sovereigns on their side very quickly overpowered the enemy, but then,
Something happened.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM
An extremely horrifying aura burst out, crushing everyone present on the battlefield, including the two Primordials, to their knees.
Yes, every being on the battlefield was neutralized.
And finally, a 2-meter-tall being, whose body seemed to be made of black, foamy material covered with endless malice, descended onto the world.
His facial features weren’t very clear; it was as if no one here was worthy of seeing his face.
"I finally caught you, you ra—"
The being spoke, his voice slow, heavy, and dreadful.
But then,
He froze.
The women he was here for...
They weren’t here.
"Where did they go!?"
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM
He screamed, releasing an aura so horrifying that—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
THUNDER THUNDER THUNDER
The world shook, instantly revealing its core as a form of submission.
What else could it do?
How could it, a low-level world, face a Transcendent?
Of course, the being didn’t come here for a mere low-level world.
With a wave of his hand, the Primordial who had hired the Leander Family rose into the air and appeared next to him, trembling.
"Where are they?"
The being questioned, his voice so menacing that the Primordial Leader could see his world shaking.
"I-I don’t know...
T-They were just h-her—"
"Just here!?
Then where did they go!?
Did they just disappear into the air!?"
"T-They m-must have teleported awa—"
"I released my aura before I came here.
They shouldn’t be able to move."
"A-Aura doesn’t seem to w-work on th—"
"Are you comparing your meager aura with mine?"
The being’s voice became even heavier.
Of course, he had also heard that aura didn’t work on those women, and since he couldn’t take any chances—because of how many times he had failed before—he wasn’t just relying on his aura.
He had also sealed away any form of spatial movement from this world.
No being could teleport away from here.
Unless, of course, that being had the complete Law of Absolute Space, and meager artifacts that simply messed with the flow of Space Laws wouldn’t work on him.
Yes, the instant Nux sensed the Transcendent’s descent, he teleported his wives away.
Yes, his wives, not him.
This man had targeted his wives—how could he let him go?
With a demonic grin on his face, he teleported both the Primordial and the Transcendent to the execution ground, an empty space surrounded by thousands of asteroids.
"W-What?"
The Primordial stuttered.
The Transcendent, on the other hand, narrowed his eyes.
"Who is it?"
He called out.
A being capable of teleporting him away without him being able to resist—especially when teleportation shouldn’t have been possible—he could tell that this being was anything but simple.
He wanted to talk it out and clear whatever misunderstanding they might have had, but—
"I’ll be the one asking."
Nux’s voice echoed throughout the surroundings, and suddenly, the space stretched endlessly.
The Laws of Space were altered, making it impossible for both the Transcendent and the Primordial to move.
’I guess I need to break through in order to deal with this one, huh?’
Nux thought in his head, but just as he considered breaking through, he paused as another idea popped into his mind.
’Can a Sovereign defeat a Transcendent?’
With a wave of his hand, he teleported next to the slave he had given the relic to.
"Give me the sword."
He ordered, and under the effect of the Slave Seal, the slave quickly passed the relic without any questions.
Nux teleported back.
It all happened in less than a few seconds.
It was more than enough time for a Transcendent-level being to do something, but right now, even a Transcendent was helpless.
Nux quickly made the connection with the relic,
Or at least, that was what he tried to do.
But before he could—
Time around him slowed down.
Even the Transcendent’s attacks, which were coming toward Nux, slowed to an absurd speed, surprising even Nux.
Then suddenly, he heard a voice.
A voice so sweet and lovely that he couldn’t believe his ears.
"Don’t be foolish, Nux Leander."

chapters.title: Chapter 1913: Holy fuck, she is beautiful!
paragraphs: Just as Nux was about to make the connection with the Relic,
Fwooosh
The time around him slowed down. Even the Transcendent’s attacks that were coming toward him slowed down, moving at a speed so slow that it almost looked like they had frozen in one place.
Nux raised his eyebrow in surprise. The surprising thing was that this seemed to have no effect on him. Well, not after his Relic was taken away.
Yes, the Relic was taken away from his very hands, and he had no idea how it happened or who did it.
Well, he had a rough idea of who did it.
The entity was the reason he was doing all this in the first place.
And finally, he heard a voice, a voice so... soothing and beautiful that he was momentarily lost.
"Don’t be foolish, Nux Leander."
Nux looked in the direction of the voice, and finally, his eyes landed on the being standing in front of him.
A being who seemed to have surpassed the concept of beauty.

A being with long black hair that seemed to represent the very concept of midnight. An obsidian veil made of pure silk covered her eyes. She wore black robes with gold patterns, a strange sort of power pulsated around her. Nux, however, couldn’t sense it at all.
His focus was all on her.
Her hourglass body that couldn’t be hidden under her robes, her veil that added a layer of mysteriousness around her, and her face that seemed nothing short of perfection.
Yes, Nux couldn’t see her complete face, but he didn’t have to.
He knew it.
She was... beautiful.
And as she stood there, in outer space, surrounded by thousands of asteroids that moved extremely slowly because of her power, her beauty was magnified to an absurd degree.
*Picture*
’Holy fuck, she is beautiful!’
Shadow didn’t fail to comment.
’Of course, it is a woman.’
Amaya rolled her eyes, already hating the woman she was seeing.
Why?
She was too beautiful!

Yes, even the Devourer, the very meaning of perfection, thought that this bitch was a little too beautiful. Almost as if she was created artificially to be the most beautiful woman in the entire Universe.
What’s worse?
This woman had been following Nux for a while now.
Yes, Nux knew someone was following him. He didn’t know who it was, what that being looked like, or how strong this being was.
He knew nothing, and it concerned him.
What concerned him even more was that he only found out about her following him after comprehending the Complete Law of Absolute Space.
What did that mean?
It meant that they didn’t know how long she had been following him.
The only thing Nux was sure about was that she couldn’t follow him to his Universe, or...
Could she but just wouldn’t?
Enjoy new chapters from freewebnovel
Nux didn’t know.
There were too many questions.
Of course, there were also a few answers, or assumptions to be more precise.
First, this woman wasn’t an enemy, at least for now.

Nux was almost one hundred percent sure this woman knew he was the Anomaly the Universe was after. If any sane person knew it, they would instantly inform the Supreme Worlds, just like Faelara did, or try to get in contact with him and use their information to their advantage.
But...
She didn’t do anything like that.
Of course, there was a possibility that she was trying to find out more about him. This was what Nux had been leaning on all this while.
However...
Nux knew he had to get in contact with her in one way or another.

With Space Law, he could sense the ’Space’ she was taking as she hid, but no matter how he tried, he couldn’t ’see’ or ’interact’ with her. Yes, he had tried it more than once. In his battle with Aeliana and the Progenitors, he randomly moved them to outer space, where she was observing him from, and rushed toward her, but every time he did that, he simply passed through her.

Nux wanted to call her out, but honestly, he didn’t even know if she was a ’her’ at that point. He just knew an entity was observing him. With such limited information, it was foolish to call her out.
So...
He came up with a plan.
Whoever it was, the entity was dead set on not revealing itself no matter what Nux did. It didn’t move, it didn’t appear, neither did it report his actions to the Supreme World.
All of this told Nux one thing:
It didn’t want attention.
And Nux decided to do just that.
Attract attention.
And what better attention could he attract than that of the Supreme Worlds themselves?
Of course, Nux wasn’t actually going to do it. It was just bait, a blind shot, a shot that worked just right.
Not to mention he also got another annoying thing he wanted to deal with using the same trap.
Nux smiled inwardly as he stared at the Transcendent, who, affected by the time flow around him, couldn’t even move.
Yes, the Transcendent didn’t come as a surprise either. Nux had noticed his presence before in other missions. He made his wives avoid all those missions, but he continued to follow them.

It was then Nux realized it. This being knew all the missions his wives had chosen. Well, not all of them, since he didn’t appear everywhere, but he was following his wives, and today, when they couldn’t avoid him anymore,
Nux decided to take on both annoyances at the same time.
Was he confident he could defeat them?
Of course not.
One was a Transcendent. Yes, with a weaker Law, but Nux still couldn’t defeat him.
As for the other...
This woman neutralized a Transcendent without even sparing him a single glance. She had been keeping an eye on him from outer space through the Universal Energy.

Of course, he still wasn’t sure if she could actually see through it, but the very fact she had been following him all this time when even the Supreme Worlds couldn’t find him told him that she was anything but simple.
Obviously, Nux couldn’t defeat either of them.

chapters.title: Chapter 1914: The Seer
paragraphs: A Transcendent and a being who could neutralize a Transcendent without even sparing him a gaze.
Obviously, Nux couldn’t defeat either of them.
Then why do something like this?
Well, because everything just... blended together.
The Transcendent was never a problem. He was one of the weaker Transcendents, a mercenary probably. The moment Nux broke through, dealing with him shouldn’t be a problem.
Even if he couldn’t, one of two Black Holes would be more than enough to deal with this weakling.
As for this woman...
Well...
She was strong.
Nux never stood a chance against her, but...
She already knew about him. He couldn’t avoid her. If she wanted to harm him, she could do it anytime she wanted to.
This woman wanted something else, and now that she was here, Nux could find out what it was.
What he did find out already was that his wives didn’t like her one bit.
’Nux! What is with you attracting all these beautiful women like nothing!? First, it was the Vampire, and the deed hasn’t even been done with her, and you already have another one lined up!’
Shadow complained.
’She is the one who has been following me, you know?’
’And? How does that change anything?’
Shadow didn’t back down.
’You go out, you attract attention.
You aren’t allowed to seduce women like this. Cover your face with a veil!’
Shadow was throwing a fit, and while she was doing that, Amaya, who was observing her, was liking her more and more.
To think there would be a day when she would like someone like Shadow.
Nux had no words.
’Why do I feel like you are reacting much more in front of her than you ever did before?’
He wondered.
’She is too beautiful!’
’Are you saying your other sisters aren’t beautiful?’
Nux chuckled.
’N-No, that’s no—’
’My wives are the most beautiful in my eyes.
Besides, you can’t even see her complete face. Who knows? She might be uglier than you think. Our imagination is often prettier than reality.’

It wasn’t just Shadow. All the women who heard his words didn’t say a word, and Nux, who could feel their emotions and knew none of them were going to fall for his words, decided to turn towards the woman in front of him instead.
It was time to continue the act.
"Who are you?"
Nux questioned as he narrowed his eyes. Doubt, suspicion, and confusion—everything could be seen on his face very clearly.
At the same time, he realized that his weapon was taken away, and he decided to return to his Universe.
It didn’t take him long to realize that he couldn’t face this woman.
The instant the woman realized what he was doing, Nux’s movements slowed down. The Time Flow around him was now affecting him as well.
What Nux found even more surprising was that the Time Flow was only affecting his physical body, not his mind.
His thoughts still moved as fast as before.
"Drop the act.
You went so far in order to meet me. Why leave when you already have me?"
As she said those words, time around Nux returned to normal, returning control of his body back to him.
The woman expected Nux to stop, but...
He didn’t.
And just as the Shadow covered his entire body, ready to leave, time around him slowed down again, and the woman sighed.
"I said drop the act, Nux Leander.

With your reaction speed, you would have reacted to my appearance a lot quicker than you did. This habit of yours—where you wait for people to react to your thought speed before making a move so that they buy your act—fails against a higher-level enemy and someone who knows you well.
And trust me when I say it,
I know you better than your wives do."
Your next read awaits at freewebnovel
The woman spoke, and in an instant, Amaya’s hate for her shot through.
And as if she could sense her hatred, the woman continued,
"Yes, Amaya Leander, I know your husband more than you do, and no, you do not have to direct your hate towards me.
I only say this because there are things the current you cannot comprehend. Even if Nux tells you everything, you wouldn’t understand.
But in the future,
You will understand it all.
You will understand the entity called Nux Leander the most."
Nux narrowed his eyes at those words.
This woman...
She was talking to Amaya through him...?
Also...
Why did her words sound so... certain?
"And you."
Then, the woman directed her attention back to Nux and,
"Drop your act.
You did all this because you wished to talk to me.
I wasn’t the one who approached you, so if you try to disappear on me again, I will not appear again."
She warned as the time around Nux returned to normal again, and this time, he stopped.
He had to give in.
He wanted to know who this woman was, and if her threat was true, and she decided not to appear in front of him again, it would become very difficult for him to find out about her.
"Who are you?"
Nux questioned directly.
At his question, the woman smiled.
"You should already know that, no?"
"I do not."
Nux shook his head, and once again, the woman sighed.
"Nux, as I said, your games might work against others, but not with me. I know what you are thinking, I know what you are trying to do, and I know what you are going to do.
You cannot hide from me."
"The Seer."
Nux called out, and the woman’s smile widened.
"It wasn’t difficult, was it?"
"Why is the most highly sought-after woman in the Universe standing here next to me?"
Nux questioned.
"Come now, weren’t you the one who wanted to meet me? You even went ahead and planned all this mess for it to work out.
Not that I blame you, of course.
You had to find out who was following you now that you finally have the ability to sense me."
The Seer then chuckled and,
"The Complete Law of Absolute Space is really too strong, huh?
Aren’t you glad you were devoured by the Black Hole?
The future you sure was."

His thoughts still moved as fast as before.
"Drop the act.
You went so far in order to meet me.
Why leave when you already have me?"
As she said those words, time around Nux returned to normal, returning control of his body back to him.
The woman expected Nux to stop, but...
He didn’t.
And just as the Shadow covered his entire body, ready to leave, time around him slowed down again, and the woman sighed.
"I said drop the act, Nux Leander.
With your reaction speed, you would have reacted to my appearance a lot quicker than you did.
This habit of yours—where you wait for people to react to your thought speed before making a move so that they buy your act—fails against a higher-level enemy and someone who knows you well.
And trust me when I say it,
I know you better than your wives do."
Your next read awaits at freewebnovel
The woman spoke, and in an instant, Amaya’s hate for her shot through.
And as if she could sense her hatred, the woman continued,
"Yes, Amaya Leander, I know your husband more than you do, and no, you do not have to direct your hate towards me.
I only say this because there are things the current you cannot comprehend.
Even if Nux tells you everything, you wouldn’t understand.
But in the future,
You will understand it all.
You will understand the entity called Nux Leander the most."
Nux narrowed his eyes at those words.
This woman...
She was talking to Amaya through him...?
Also...
Why did her words sound so... certain?
"And you."
Then, the woman directed her attention back to Nux and,
"Drop your act.
You did all this because you wished to talk to me.
I wasn’t the one who approached you, so if you try to disappear on me again, I will not appear again."
She warned as the time around Nux returned to normal again, and this time, he stopped.
He had to give in.
He wanted to know who this woman was, and if her threat was true, and she decided not to appear in front of him again, it would become very difficult for him to find out about her.
"Who are you?"
Nux questioned directly.
At his question, the woman smiled.
"You should already know that, no?"
"I do not."
Nux shook his head, and once again, the woman sighed.
"Nux, as I said, your games might work against others, but not with me.
I know what you are thinking, I know what you are trying to do, and I know what you are going to do.
You cannot hide from me."
"The Seer."
Nux called out, and the woman’s smile widened.
"It wasn’t difficult, was it?"
"Why is the most highly sought-after woman in the Universe standing here next to me?"
Nux questioned.
"Come now, weren’t you the one who wanted to meet me?
You even went ahead and planned all this mess for it to work out.
Not that I blame you, of course.
You had to find out who was following you now that you finally have the ability to sense me."
The Seer then chuckled and,
"The Complete Law of Absolute Space is really too strong, huh?
Aren’t you glad you were devoured by the Black Hole?
The future you sure was."

She added.
"What does that mean?"
"You wouldn’t understand."
"Try me."
"I already did. This is why I am telling you."
The Seer smiled.
"Huh?"
Nux frowned in confusion.
"Why are you so confused? You should already know about me after devouring Umbrasol, don’t you?"
Nux was silent.
Seeing his silence, the Seer chuckled again.
"Come on, Nux Leander.
Your next chapter awaits on freewebnovel
There is no point. Or did you forget what they say about me?"
Nux stayed silent, but this time, the Seer just looked at him with a smile, as if waiting for something.
Nux knew exactly what she wanted, and the problem was... she knew that Nux knew what she wanted, so she was already expecting it.
In the end, Nux had no choice but to give in.
"The woman who knows everything."
He muttered, and the Seer’s smile widened.
"I don’t believe it."
"I don’t believe it."
Both Nux and the Seer spoke at the same time, and as Nux frowned, the Seer just smiled knowingly.
"I know everything, and that includes you.
Your past, your present, and your future.
I know it all.
I know what you are going to say, do, or think.
Nothing,
Nothing is hidden from my eyes, Nux Leander."
The woman spoke in a low voice that radiated confidence so unshakable that it felt Absolute.
"So when I say you wouldn’t understand, I say this because I know you wouldn’t.
And when I say I already ’tried you’ as you wanted me to, it is because in a certain timeline, I did, and I was proved to be right."
"So you have the ability to see possible futures?"
Nux questioned, trying to make sense of this conversation.
The Seer, however, shook her head.
"I have the ability to see everything.
Future, present, and past.
I have control over time itself."
"So you can travel to the future or past?"
"No, I am a living entity. I cannot do that."
"What can you do then?"
Nux frowned.
"This is why I said you wouldn’t understand."
"Woman."
Nux called out.
He had had enough.
"If you already know everything, you should know that the way you talk is annoying me."
The Seer chuckled at those words.
"Why do you think I am talking like this?"
Her tone changed, sounding more playful and cheerful. It sounded much more... open.
"I won’t get a lot of chances to do this in the future,
so I am enjoying whatever time I have."
Again, her words were confusing. Nux, however, could sense a form of... attachment in those words.
Something that confused him.
"You seem to be enjoying this conversation."
He commented.
"And I know I am the only one who is out of all of us."
The Seer smiled.
"Amaya must be fuming."
Again, Nux turned silent.
He didn’t know what he was supposed to say here.
"You know everything, don’t you?"
"So you want me to somehow explain what I am to you?"
"You should know a way, no?"
Nux asked shamelessly, and the Seer laughed out loud.
"I do not exist in time."
"What...?"
Nux raised an eyebrow.
"Past, present, or the future, I can see it all, but I do not exist anywhere.
Consider this to be a curse, a curse of knowledge that I once pursued during the time when I didn’t... know."
"So the Seer..."
"An entity named the Seer does not exist in the Universe.
I am merely a concept in people’s minds.
A being they know about but... at the same time, they do not."
"But you are right in front of me. How do you not exist?"
Nux couldn’t understand.
He knew a lot of things, but this...
This... he couldn’t understand.
"You talk as if you exist."
The Seer laughed.
"Hah?"
Nux had no clue what this woman was talking about. It almost felt like she had lost her mind and was blabbering whatever came to her mind.
But despite that...
Her words... her voice...
They all had a certain charm to them, a charm he couldn’t ignore.
A charm that... attracted him towards her?
For some reason, he felt like he had a connection with her, a connection he didn’t... remember.
Or more precisely, a connection that hadn’t formed yet.
Suddenly, the Seer extended her hands towards Nux and,
"Come with me."
Tempted, Nux held her hand. He didn’t know why, but his movements were very gentle, as if he didn’t wish to hurt her.
It was something that placed a light smile on the Seer’s face. Then, she stepped forward, and Nux realized that they were in an entirely different place.
He extended his spatial senses and realized that they were about a couple of light-years away from where they stood.
This woman...
She teleported!
To be able to teleport so far away, the amount of energy required was absurd! Even he could only do it because of the Astral Bond he had with the stars inside his universe.
"You are wrong.
It is not teleportation."
Knowing what he was thinking, the Seer corrected him, and Nux’s expression changed as he realized it.
"You altered the flow of time to increase your speed."
"Well..."
The Seer thought about it for a moment, considered how to say it in a way Nux would understand, and then,
"I raised the flow of time between two spaces. I didn’t increase my speed, I just walked, and the distance that should have taken us billions of years to cover took a second."
Nux just blinked continuously and decided to ignore the words he just heard.
"Why are we here?"
He questioned directly, and the Seer pointed at the world in front of them.
"See that?
That’s the World of Titans, Colossa, a High-Level World."
"And?"
"And we are going to go in."

chapters.title: Chapter 1916: You are... quite daring, huh...
paragraphs: "See that?
That’s the World of Titans, Colossa, a High-Level World."
The Seer spoke as she pointed at the giant world in front of them.
"And?"
"And we are going to go in."
"What...?"
Nux blinked in surprise.
The woman, however, didn’t give him the time to think, and she walked.
Fwoosh
Just like before, with just a single step, or at least that is what it felt like, Nux and she were right in front of Colossa’s boundary.
"I don’t think it i-"
Nux tried to warn, but then, the Seer simply walked in, and with a single step, they were in Colossa, inside a castle so huge that even Nux was taken aback.
"Where is this?"
He questioned with a curious look on his face.
"Gaea Prime, the home to the Giant Progenitor, an Eternal-Level Being."
The Seer introduced, and Nux’s eyes widened.
"W-We are in front of the Giant Progenitor’s house?"
"Mhm."
’Crazy! This woman’s absolutely crazy!’
Shadow shouted, she was in utter disbelief.
’Wait...’
Then suddenly, Amaya frowned.
’Why is no one coming to them?’
She questioned, and the moment she did, the rest of the women’s expressions changed.
Normally, a Progenitor would instantly be able to tell when a foreign entity visits their world because the World’s Will would inform them about the intruders.
Nux never had this problem since he didn’t belong to this Universe. Right now, however, he was with someone else. The very fact that no one had approached them yet meant...
Vyriana called out as she narrowed her eyes.
Nux, however, was already looking at the Seer, and the woman smiled.
"Do you understand what I was trying to say before?"
"You do not exist in this Universe..."
Nux realized.
"Just like you."
The Seer added.
"Then are you..."
It was for a very minute moment, but Nux slipped up. He, however, controlled himself, and before he could ask if she was another Universe, he stopped himself.
But...
"No, I am not an independent Universe like you."
Nux’s expression changed.
She knew...
The Seer ignored his change. It was something she expected, so she wasn’t surprised, not that she was ever surprised by anything.
"I am not breaking any ’rules’ because those rules do not exist for me.
I am not the Anomaly the Universe or the Supreme Worlds are after."
She chuckled.
Read exclusive chapters at freewebnovel
"The Supreme Worlds...?"
Nux raised his eyebrow.
"Ah, right.
You still don’t know."
The Seer realized.
"The Supreme Worlds know about you.
Well, not you, they know about the Anomaly the Universe is after, and they are looking for you.
They even put aside their arrogance and contacted me to look for you,
So they are quite serious about it."
The woman then looked at Nux and,
"So be careful, one mistake and..."
She didn’t have to complete those words. Nux understood what she meant and nodded with a solemn look on his face.

"Anyways, as I am saying, I do not exist in this Universe. Of course, the fundamental reason behind why that is the case is very different from yours, but at least in that regard, we are quite similar."
She smiled.
Nux stared at the woman for a while, then he questioned,
"You seem to know a lot about the Supreme Worlds."
The Seer just smiled as she tilted her head.
Nux realized his mistake,
"Right, you know everything."
Soon, however, he shook his head and,
"No, I mean, you seem to have a relationship with the Supreme Worlds, to think they actively contacted you and requested you to look for me."
"Well, they didn’t exactly make a request."
The Seer chuckled.
"They are quite arrogant right now."
"Right now...?"
Nux raised his eyebrows at those words.
She talked as if this would change in the future.
The Seer, however, just smiled, not explaining anything anymore.
Nux, however, didn’t let it go.
"So? Are you here to take me to them?"
He questioned, and she just stared at him, acting somewhat offended.
"Stop playing these games, will you? Just ask what you wish to ask. I never said I will not answer any of your questions."
"Why are you helping me?"
Nux questioned directly, doing exactly what the woman wanted him to.
"I am returning a favor."
The Seer smiled.
"A favor."
"You wouldn’t unders-"
"Oh, come on!"
"Hahaha~"
The Seer laughed at his outburst. Her laughter was so... melodious, and in an instant, Nux’s frustration flushed out.
And as if she knew that, the woman looked up, as if staring at the purple sky, and,
"Let’s just say I am choosing sides."
"Aren’t you choosing the weaker side?"
Nux questioned, looking at the sky as well.
"I know you don’t mean that."
"I don’t."
Nux laughed.
"Another question."
"Why didn’t I take you to one of the Supreme Worlds and come to Colossa instead?"
The Seer guessed Nux’s next question.
Well, not really a guess, but whatever.
Nux nodded after a slight pause.
"You cannot meet an Infinity right now."
She spoke, and in an instant, Nux recalled how Azriel had said the same thing.
"Why?"
He questioned.
"They will see through you in an instant."
"They will know I am a Universe?"
Nux questioned, and suddenly, the Seer paused. She turned towards Nux again and smiled,
"You are opening up to me."
"Answer my question."
Nux ordered.
"They will know you are the Anomaly."
"And Universe?"
"No, most of them do not understand the concept of another Universe."
"There are concepts even they do not understand?"
"There are a lot of things they do not understand."
"Like?"
At his question, the Seer smiled again.
"You wouldn’t understand either."
"This is really annoying, you know."
"I do."
The Seer chuckled again.
She seemed to be really enjoying their conversation.
"So if I enter the Supreme World, they will be able to sense me?"
"Yes."
She nodded.
"What about you? Would they be able to sense you?"
"Trying to gauge my strength, eh?"
She chuckled.
"You dont’ have to answer if you do not want to."
Nux didn’t wish to pressure her. She, however, just shrugged.
"They wouldn’t."
She then chuckled and,
"Most of the time, I am hiding right in that absurdly stupid meeting hall, and they are searching the entire Universe, trying to find me.
It is quite funny, actually."
"You are... quite daring, huh..."
"Well, they wouldn’t exactly be able to hurt me even if they did find me, so I have that assurance to be daring."
She shrugged with absolute confidence, and Nux just... he just looked at her laughing at the supposedly strongest force in this Universe, and he had no clue how to react.

chapters.title: Chapter 1918: She is lying.
paragraphs: ’She’s strong, beautiful, and resourceful.
She knows everything, she seems to be on your side, and has even prepared a meeting gift for you.
So Nux...
Why do you not trust her?’
Shadow questioned as she sensed Nux’s distrust when he talked to her.
Yes, all the emotions Nux showed, the inexplicable attachment, that connection, and whatnot, it was all an act.
During their entire conversation, never once did Nux’s feeling of distrust disappear or even thin out. Rather, it continued to grow.
And this confused Shadow.
Not just her, it confused the rest of the women too, even Amaya.
After all, with how the women acted, they felt like the Seer had some sort of connection with Nux in the future. Possibly, she was, or in this case, would be one of his wives in the future.

She even appeared and stopped Nux from using the Relic that would alert the World of Eternity. She also didn’t give in to the Supreme Worlds’ demand when they wanted her to find him and told him everything he wanted to know, or he could know.
Then why?
Why the distrust?
And why such apparent distrust?

The women would have understood if Nux was just being cautious; it aligned with his nature. When someone with so much power approaches him, regardless of their intentions, he is always cautious of them.
Heck, he is less cautious in front of his enemies than those who appear to be his allies. Even in front of Azriel, he had never once truly let his guard down. But this...
This seemed different.
Nux wasn’t being cautious of her like he usually is with Azriel, he was...

He was feeling emotions he would usually feel while dealing with an enemy. Even in the case of Vulpiana, when he was distrustful of her and planned everything out, he didn’t feel such intense distrust.
It was almost as if...
’She plans to betray us.’
Nux answered, and the women all frowned in absolute confusion.
’How do you know that?’
Amaya questioned directly. After all, she didn’t catch anything odd. Rather... she had started to... accept her.
Yes, if it wasn’t for Nux’s constant distrust that she felt, she might have already accepted that woman as her future sister.
’Maybe that is an oddity in itself?’
Amaya wondered in her head.
Right now, however, she was still confused. She wanted to know what made Nux think this way. She wanted to know what he saw that she didn’t. She wanted to know what she missed.
’The way she talked, I felt like she knew me.’
Nux started, and the rest of the women nodded; they felt the same.
’I felt like I had some sort of strong connection with her, possibly in the future.’
The women nodded again.
’Possibly, she will become one of my wives in the future.’
And again, the women nodded.
Then suddenly, Nux returned to his Universe and appeared in front of his wives.
"Tell me, what is it that I desire the most? My true goal, a goal I have been working for all this while?"
"To become so strong that no threat could hurt you or us and making it so that we live in this Universe for eternity with no being or entity bothering us."
Felberta answered.
This was something everyone knew.
The end goal was the same since the very beginning, and it wasn’t just Nux’s goal alone, it was the goal they all shared.
Nux nodded at his first wife, then he continued,
"And if we do get what we desire,
What are we going to do next?"
"Live happily forever?"
Felberta answered.
This was something very obvious.
Did it sound boring?
They were with Nux, nothing around him was boring. They could spend eternity with him.
"And?"
Nux continued,
"What else?
No, let me make this clearer,
What would you do once we get what we desire?"
"Stay together with you...?"
Felberta answered with a frown.
Not because she wasn’t sure, but because she was confused as to why Nux was asking something so obvious.
"Would any of you return to the time you didn’t meet me and change anything?"
"No."
Amaya was the first to answer.
"My experiences were what made me and led to my encounter with you. I love who I am right now because I know you love me.
I wouldn’t change that in any way."
The other women nodded as well.
They all thought the same. Then suddenly, Amaya realized what Nux was trying to say.
"You do not trust her because she came to you?"
"I know none of my wives would ever do.
Even if you have the power to return to time, you would only do it if you have any regrets, and if you, as my wives, have any regrets, it means that I failed as your husband."
Nux’s eyes then shined brightly, and,

"And if there is one thing I am certain about, it is that I will never fail as a husband. I will always be the man who loves you the most, and I will shower you all with so much love that you will never hate anything about yourselves, even your traumas or regrets.
The very fact that she appeared in front of me discredits her untold story."
"But she did say she didn’t come from the future. What if she just saw the possibility of you and her being together and decided to come meet you? I know I might do that.
I can see myself sabotaging my own future self if it means I get to meet and stay with you."
Amaya spoke, declaring her love in a manner so messed up that one couldn’t tell what’s right and what’s wrong anymore.
"There is also a possibility that we weren’t able to get what we desired in one of the possible futures she saw and... decided to help you and get close to you at the same time."
Felberta answered, thinking of a scenario where she would do the same too.
Discover hidden content at Freewebnovel
Nux, however, shook his head.
"What you are doing is putting yourself in her stead,
But...
You aren’t her.
She is... a different form of existence.
And if what she says is true, then she is either lying, or there is something I do not understand here and I believe it is the former."
Nux replied, and his wives just stared at him in silence.
None of them knew what he was trying to say, and Nux, who knew that, thought of a way to explain it.

chapters.title: Chapter 1919: It’s a waste of time.
paragraphs: "What you are doing is putting yourself in her stead,
But...
You aren’t her.
She is... a different form of existence.
And if what she says is true, then she is either lying, or there is something I do not understand here, and I believe it is the former."
The women just stared at him in silence, and Nux, who knew what they were thinking, continued his explanation.
"Think about all this from this perspective,
Why now?"
The women narrowed their eyes.
"We know that she has been observing me for a long time now, and not once did she appear in front of us before. Why did she only appear when I was able to sense her?"
"You called her, didn’t you?"
Shadow questioned. This time, however, Amaya stayed silent.
Now, she was slowly understanding what Nux was trying to say.
"I arranged everything in order to lure her out," Nux admitted.
"According to me, the ’entity’ who was observing me didn’t want any attention, so it would stop me from using the Eternity’s Relic, and that is what she did.
That is what any normal being stalking me would do,
But...
She supposedly knew everything about me. She should know I would never attract a Supreme World’s attention on my own. She should know all of it was just an act. She had no reason to come out."
"She said it herself, didn’t she? She just came out because you wanted to meet her," Shadow answered.
"You think there would be a time when I wouldn’t want to meet a beautiful stalker who had been keeping an eye on me for such a long time?"
Nux questioned as he tilted his head.
Shadow turned silent.
"As someone who knows me the most, she should know that I would always appreciate her approaching me on her own rather than me finding out about her myself."
Then, a frown appeared on Nux’s face as he stared at his wives and,
"Do none of you find it odd that she appeared right after I found out about her existence?"
He couldn’t understand.
Was he looking too deep into it? Did Vulpiana’s actions affect him more than he thought?
Nux wouldn’t lie; it was a possibility. His reaction, his... apparent distrust, might have been fueled by Vulpiana, but...
But in no world did Nux believe that that woman wasn’t at least a little bit suspicious. Something was definitely wrong about her, and he knew he wasn’t the only one who had such thoughts.
He stared at Amaya, who had lowered her head, and called her out,
"Amaya."
He could sense Amaya’s emotions—doubt, suspicion, and confusion. He could sense it all.
"What if... this was the right time?"
After a small pause, Amaya came up with an alternate theory. For the first time in her life, she was trying to defend a woman who clearly seemed interested in her husband.
Nux frowned at her question, and the Devourer elaborated,
"If she knows you, then it must mean you two would have encountered each other at some point in the future.
What if that happened after you got the ability to sense her?
What if in the future, while you were roaming around the Universe, you managed to sense her existence, and, curious as to how someone at your level managed to do that, she appeared in front of you?
What if today was the day of your fateful encounter?
After all, she did wait for 10 years before finally appearing in front of you.
What if, unlike what we are accusing her of, she is simply trying to follow through with the events that were supposed to happen in order to not ruin her relationship with you?"
This time, Nux was the one who turned silent, and the Devourer didn’t stop.
"It would make sense, no?
Even if you recall your conversation with her,
She didn’t exactly reveal anything big.
She only told you she was the Seer, then she answered some of your questions, and then asked you to let her meet Lord Azriel.
All those things would have happened even if you were meeting for the first time and she had no prior information regarding you.
What if she made sure your first meeting went exactly like it was supposed to?"
Amaya completed, and Nux paused for a moment.
"...so what you are saying is that this is how our meeting was supposed to go?"
"Well, not exactly, since it wasn’t natural and was arranged by her, but to some extent, yes. At the very least, this should create fewer deviations in the future."
Amaya shrugged; she didn’t know how time worked, so she wasn’t sure.
"Your theory has one problem."
"What?"
"This could never have been the day of our fateful encounter."
"Why?"

"I spent the last 10 years in Yrniel. We only returned to Outer Space a few months ago, and ever since I found out about the Transcendent following Astaria and others, I have never once left their side.
I didn’t exactly have the time to roam around the Universe."
"There is also a possibility that she found you when the Supreme Worlds told her to but was intrigued by your existence and followed you.
You, who sensed her, did everything you did right now, and that led to your fateful encounter.
If this is the case, then your encounter with her today was even closer to what was supposed to happen originally."
Another possibility.
"But then this changes all the conversations we were supposed to have," Nux answered.

"She would ask all sorts of questions like, ’How did you find me? How did you appear next to me?’ Blah blah. If she wanted to keep our first encounter similar to how it was supposed to be, she would have acted surprised by my appearance—something that shouldn’t be difficult for someone like her."
"What if—"
"Amaya, listen to me."
In the end, Nux called out.
"We can sit here all day and discuss millions or billions of possibilities of what was supposed to happen and what did happen, but the problem remains the same.
We do not understand Time.
We do not understand what sort of existence that woman is.
You can continue to come up with a certain possibility, and I’ll probably come up with a way to counter it.
It’s a waste of time.
Let me trust my instincts on this one."

"According to me, the ’entity’ who was observing me didn’t want any attention, so it would stop me from using the Eternity’s Relic, and that is what she did.
That is what any normal being stalking me would do,
But...
She supposedly knew everything about me.
She should know I would never attract a Supreme World’s attention on my own.
She should know all of it was just an act.
She had no reason to come out."
"She said it herself, didn’t she?
She just came out because you wanted to meet her," Shadow answered.
"You think there would be a time when I wouldn’t want to meet a beautiful stalker who had been keeping an eye on me for such a long time?"
Nux questioned as he tilted his head.
Shadow turned silent.
"As someone who knows me the most, she should know that I would always appreciate her approaching me on her own rather than me finding out about her myself."
Then, a frown appeared on Nux’s face as he stared at his wives and,
"Do none of you find it odd that she appeared right after I found out about her existence?"
He couldn’t understand.
Was he looking too deep into it?
Did Vulpiana’s actions affect him more than he thought?
Nux wouldn’t lie; it was a possibility.
His reaction, his... apparent distrust, might have been fueled by Vulpiana, but...
But in no world did Nux believe that that woman wasn’t at least a little bit suspicious.
Something was definitely wrong about her, and he knew he wasn’t the only one who had such thoughts.
He stared at Amaya, who had lowered her head, and called her out,
"Amaya."
He could sense Amaya’s emotions—doubt, suspicion, and confusion.
He could sense it all.
"What if... this was the right time?"
After a small pause, Amaya came up with an alternate theory.
For the first time in her life, she was trying to defend a woman who clearly seemed interested in her husband.
Nux frowned at her question, and the Devourer elaborated,
"If she knows you, then it must mean you two would have encountered each other at some point in the future.
What if that happened after you got the ability to sense her?
What if in the future, while you were roaming around the Universe, you managed to sense her existence, and, curious as to how someone at your level managed to do that, she appeared in front of you?
What if today was the day of your fateful encounter?
After all, she did wait for 10 years before finally appearing in front of you.
What if, unlike what we are accusing her of, she is simply trying to follow through with the events that were supposed to happen in order to not ruin her relationship with you?"
This time, Nux was the one who turned silent, and the Devourer didn’t stop.
"It would make sense, no?
Even if you recall your conversation with her,
She didn’t exactly reveal anything big.
She only told you she was the Seer, then she answered some of your questions, and then asked you to let her meet Lord Azriel.
All those things would have happened even if you were meeting for the first time and she had no prior information regarding you.
What if she made sure your first meeting went exactly like it was supposed to?"
Amaya completed, and Nux paused for a moment.
"...so what you are saying is that this is how our meeting was supposed to go?"
"Well, not exactly, since it wasn’t natural and was arranged by her, but to some extent, yes.
At the very least, this should create fewer deviations in the future."
Amaya shrugged; she didn’t know how time worked, so she wasn’t sure.
"Your theory has one problem."
"What?"
"This could never have been the day of our fateful encounter."
"Why?"
"I spent the last 10 years in Yrniel.
We only returned to Outer Space a few months ago, and ever since I found out about the Transcendent following Astaria and others, I have never once left their side.
I didn’t exactly have the time to roam around the Universe."
"There is also a possibility that she found you when the Supreme Worlds told her to but was intrigued by your existence and followed you.
You, who sensed her, did everything you did right now, and that led to your fateful encounter.
If this is the case, then your encounter with her today was even closer to what was supposed to happen originally."
Another possibility.
"But then this changes all the conversations we were supposed to have," Nux answered.
"She would ask all sorts of questions like, ’How did you find me?
How did you appear next to me?’ Blah blah.
If she wanted to keep our first encounter similar to how it was supposed to be, she would have acted surprised by my appearance—something that shouldn’t be difficult for someone like her."
"What if—"
"Amaya, listen to me."
In the end, Nux called out.
"We can sit here all day and discuss millions or billions of possibilities of what was supposed to happen and what did happen, but the problem remains the same.
We do not understand Time.
We do not understand what sort of existence that woman is.
You can continue to come up with a certain possibility, and I’ll probably come up with a way to counter it.
It’s a waste of time.
Let me trust my instincts on this one."

chapters.title: Chapter 1920: He would still... choose his wives.
paragraphs: "We can sit here all day and discuss millions or billions of possibilities of what was supposed to happen and what did happen, but the problem remains the same.
We do not understand Time.
We do not understand what sort of existence that woman is.
You can continue to come up with a certain possibility, and I’ll probably come up with a way to counter it.
It’s a waste of time.
Let me trust my instincts with this one."
He spoke with a serious look on his face.
Then a smile appeared on his face and,
"And I know you aren’t trying to defend her. You couldn’t care less about other women; you simply wish to understand me and my thought process.
So I’ll give you a possibility of my own.
One day, I attracted that woman’s attention. Maybe it was indeed when I destroyed all those worlds ten years ago, or maybe...
It was way before."
Nux spoke, and as the rest of the women turned towards him, he continued,
"Maybe it was when that father of mine appeared next to me. After all, a being from a once-destroyed Supreme World came to a mere Saint; that ought to attract attention."
The women’s expressions changed, and Nux chuckled.

"Since then, she kept an eye on me, trying to find out everything there was about me. She eavesdropped on our conversations and thought of doing it till she found out everything about me so she could put up her little act.
But now, since I sensed her existence, she decided to stop hiding and started her act."
Nux then glanced at his wives and,
"So the reason she appeared was because she had no other choice. She never expected me to find her."
"But she already expected you to be able to sense her, didn’t she?"
"And how do we know that? Who’s to say she wasn’t just alerted by the times I intentionally tried teleporting next to her but failed to find her?"
Nux questioned, and Shadow turned silent.
"So you are saying...
She is not the Seer?"
"I wouldn’t be too sure."
Nux shrugged.
"But she... went to a High-Level World, and they couldn’t find her."
"That doesn’t exactly prove that she is the Seer. And even if she is the Seer who is supposed to know everything,
How can we be sure that the Seer knows everything about me too?"
"What...?"
Amaya frowned.
"If she were the all-knowing Seer, she had no reason to observe us, did she? She would have already known everything she wanted to know without having to stalk us."
"But you were the one who said that the Seer knew everything..."
Evane muttered.
"She might know everything about us, but not us.
That could also be the reason why she is so interested in us."
"Why would she not know about u—"
Amaya wanted to question; she, however, stopped in the middle as she realized something.
"We do not belong to the Universe."
"Exactly."
Nux smiled.
"The Seer knows everything and every being in this Universe.
But what about the beings who aren’t a part of this Universe?
Even the very Universe cannot sense our existence.
What if...
We aren’t even in those millions or billions of possibilities she sees?
What if... just like the Universe, we are anomalies for her too? Factors that she cannot calculate or see—hindrances even?
That would very much give her the reason to approach us and find out everything about us, no?"
Nux questioned, and the women started thinking with solemn looks on their faces.
"But... if we are a hindrance to her...
Why not kill us?
She very much has the capability to do it, doesn’t she?"
"Who knows?
Maybe she has some use for us?
Or maybe...
She is actually an ally."
The women stared at him with deadpan looks on their faces.
"What? Don’t look at me like that.
As I said, all of this is just us guessing the possibilities. It is no different than a bored man’s ramblings since we have no proof to back our statements.
The only sane conclusion from this conversation is that,
My gut tells me not to trust her.
So I will not.
I do not want any more betrayals."
Nux declared, and the women stared at him in silence.
"And what next?"
Suddenly, Vyriana questioned.
"What are we going to do now? She wants us to talk to Lord Azriel? Are we going to do that?"
"Of course."
Nux nodded.
"We will...?"
"Do we have any other choice?"
Nux looked at his wives and,
"That woman knows our secret. She has and had the power to get rid of us anytime she wished. She is the last person we can go against right now.
Especially right now, when not all of us can be safe inside our Universe."
Nux still hadn’t formed a connection with the rest of his wives. If things went bad, he couldn’t pull them all into his Universe and protect them.
The last thing he wanted right now was to offend a being who not only knew his secret but also knew where it would hurt him the most.
He would do what he was told to.
"Maybe... she predicted this conversation as well..."
Amaya muttered in a weak voice.
"Maybe she predicted your suspicion and still appeared because she knew you would do exactly what she wants you to..."
"Maybe."
Nux nodded.
"Who knows? We are dealing with a being even the Supreme Worlds have no control over. Anything can be a possibility."
The women nodded, their faces solemn.
"Haaaaahh..."
Nux exhaled deeply. Then, he stretched his body, and a wide smile appeared on his face.
"It is time to get that old man involved. Letting him sleep peacefully never felt good anyway.
I wanted to annoy someone, and he’s the perfect target."
"What about Aeliana?"
Vyriana questioned, and Nux froze, his expression serious.
"...I’ll talk to her first."
"What if she says no?"
Nux turned silent, his body trembling.
He couldn’t say it out loud, but deep down, he knew the answer.
He would still... choose his wives.
