"You can have your turn after me."
Aeliana bribed her friend, to which the Dragon agreed very quickly.
"What about me?"
The Heart of the Universe questioned.
"You after her."
The Vampire bribed her as well.
"Alright."
Of course, Shadow wasn't going to let the chance go.
But then,
BOOOOOOOOOOM
Another extremely powerful Aura burst out and suddenly, an absurd amount of Devouring Energy gathered around the area, instantly devouring the Power of Control that had slowed Amaya down.
Yes, her jealousy pushed Amaya Leander to break through as well.
And her first words after becoming a Primordial was...
"Get away, bitch."
"You come after h-"
"Get Away.
Bitch."

The Devourer repeated as she forcefully separated Nux and Aeliana, before wrapping herself around HER husband and surrounding themselves with Devouring Energy, that devoured the very concept of time itself, giving the two of them infinite amount of time to do whatever they wanted.
Yes, the Devourer couldn't control herself any further.
Nux was hers and HERS alone.

chapters.title: Chapter 1945 Give me some time, I will end him myself.
paragraphs: In the corner of the Vast Universe, a being with long black hair was hovering in Outer Space, surrounded by Universal Energy that was no different than poison to others.

This poison, however, didn't seem to have any effect on this being. Rather, this being was absorbing this poison and getting stronger and stronger at a rate so scary that even the strongest beings in the Universe would feel alarmed by it.
The being was handsome, extremely handsome. With his body hovering in the air, he seemed no different than a God. He had a serene look on his face, but suddenly, a slight frown appeared.
"Hmm?"
He opened his eyes.
"Are you saying he is attacking my world?"
He muttered. It was almost as if he was talking to himself.
Soon, however, his expression turned even grimmer.
"To think he would choose a time when I cannot protect my world..."
The being clenched his fists, frustrated.
He wanted nothing more than to return and protect his world, but...
"I cannot go."
He shook his head, calming his intense emotions down.
"If he senses my presence, he might devour me too, and if he does that...
He will become too strong."
The being knew his importance. He was now connected to the Universe's Will. He was the Universe's Chosen. The Universe's Child.
If the Anomaly devoured him, it would gain a part of the Universe's Will and become too strong. Stopping him would be impossible if that happened.
"You want to devour Yrniel?"
The being frowned. He still seemed like he was talking to himself, as if he had lost his mind.
"And what do you think would happen then? How many worlds have you destroyed trying to catch him? Has it succeeded before? What makes you think it would succeed now?"
The being questioned, and then suddenly, a cruel look appeared on his face.
"Don't worry. This time, you aren't the only one that bastard has challenged. He is now against me.
Give me some time,
I will end him myself."
Silence fell in the area.

The being continued to stare in a certain direction, his crimson eyes shining threateningly, but then, as if the cruel expression he had shown was fake, his face returned to normal and... he closed his eyes.
As if this matter didn't bother him anymore.
Time passed. The being continued to absorb the Universal Energy, getting stronger and stronger with each passing second.
The being continued to hover in space, unbothered by anything around him. The very Universal Energy hid his existence. Even if a being walked right past him, that being wouldn't be able to sense him.
He had nothing to worry about and could cultivate in peace without having to worry about anything.
But then...
The space around him trembled, and once again, a frown appeared on his handsome face.
"Again?"
He muttered, his frown deepening.
"Take me there."
He spoke, and suddenly, his body dematerialized, as if it was engulfed by the very Universe.
The being then materialized in Yrniel, where the Anomaly was supposed to be creating a mess. However, the instant he appeared here...
His expression changed.
"I do not see anything."
Yrniel was... peaceful.
This was completely out of expectations.
After all, the Leaders of this world had disappeared. There should be chaos all over the place.
"No, I do not see anything. There is no sign of the Anomaly."
Azriel muttered again, his expression grim.
"Did he leave?"
He wondered.
"Did he know I would be coming here?
But how...?"
The Universe's Child couldn't understand.
Then, a determined look appeared on his face as he realized something.
"He will come again."
He muttered.
"He is targeting this place because of your connection to me. I cannot let this happen anymore.
I will create another shield."
Azriel spoke as he hovered in the air.
The space around him trembled again, and suddenly, his expression changed.
"You will?"
He blinked in surprise, and very quickly, a light smirk appeared on his face.
"20,000 years would be enough."
Azriel muttered as suddenly,
BOOOOOOOOOOOM
Yrniel's energy levels shot up.
In an instant, every being in this world passed out. Yrniel's Will itself flickered in surprise and appeared in front of Azriel.
A gentle smile appeared on Azriel's face as he sensed the familiar energy.
Yrniel had finally absorbed all the energy he had released, but now, its energy was rising even further. It was something that even Yrniel found surprising.
"The Universe is giving you the energy required to create a third shield.
This will protect you from that darned Anomaly until I am strong enough to take him down."
Azriel revealed.
Yrniel's core flickered, and despite not being connected to it any longer, he could feel its joy.
The Universe's Child smiled at that. Then, he stared at the white ball hovering in front of him and,
"Give birth to new Progenitors. This time, distribute the powers evenly so they can become strong enough to protect you in the future. Don't rely on just one."
Yrniel's core flickered at those words, and Azriel nodded.
"Stop worrying. I am not going anywhere. I will still be here to protect you.
This shield won't affect me, so I will continue to visit.
This is not a goodbye."
The core flickered again, and after Azriel nodded at it one last time,
Flicker
It flickered even more violently as suddenly,
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The entire world shook.
BOOOOOM

A vast amount of energy exploded out of the white ball hovering in front of Azriel, instantly covering the entire world. Then, the energy solidified, forming what seemed like a transparent barrier around him.
Bzztt
The transparent barrier flickered more than once. Azriel patiently watched the entire process. He could also sense the numerous eyes that were attracted towards Yrniel.
It was the beings from the Middle-Level World in this sector.
Sensing something strange happening to one of their subordinate worlds, they all gathered and expanded their senses.
But then, Azriel closed his eyes, and all of Yrniel was surrounded by Universal Energy, blocking all the prying eyes and at the same time, giving an impression that Yrniel was about to be devoured.
Bzztt
Five minutes later, after one last flicker, the barrier solidified itself. The Universal Energy surrounding Yrniel disappeared together with Yrniel.
And just like that,
Yrniel hid itself from the rest of the Universe for the third time.

chapters.title: Chapter 1946 Nux Leander! I will kill you!!
paragraphs: "It's gone..."
Aeliana muttered as she hovered in the space, staring at the empty void where Yrniel once stood.
Nux appeared behind her and placed his hand on her shoulder.
"On a positive note, now there's nothing holding us back.
We are no longer people who came from a world named Yrniel, after all, Yrniel doesn't exist anymore.
We are now the Anomaly.
Beings with no origin."
Aeliana's grin widened at those words.
"We can participate in any wars, devour any world, and do whatever we want, and nothing would be traced back to Yrniel."
The Vampire muttered.
"Indeed.
The true fun begins now."
"It really does, doesn't it?"
The couple then heard another voice.
"Mother."
Nux smiled as he stared at his mother.
"I feel so... powerful."
Faustina muttered as she clenched her fists.
Honestly, she had become weaker than before, but for the first time in such a long time... she had something to look forward to.
She was no longer stuck at an incomplete cultivation stage, with a weak foundation and no hopes of getting any stronger.
Now, with her very foundation rebuilt in the strongest, the most sturdy way possible, the sky was the limit.
She could feel it.
Her almost endless potential,
The possibility of reaching a level much stronger than what she could imagine.
The possibility of being able to grow again.
It was a powerful feeling.
And the one who made this possible was currently standing in front of her, her son.
"That is good."
Nux smiled gently as he stared at his mother.
"But be careful."
Then, he warned.

"I only turned you all into Primordials because that was the only way for you to survive. I even strengthened your Law in the process, but you need to understand that while the Law you have may be stronger, your understanding of it is only at the level of a Sovereign.
You were pushed to Primordial by a foreign power without a proper understanding of your Law.
If you do not stabilize your foundation right here, the domain you would form when you become Transcendent would be much weaker than others."
"I understand."
Faustina nodded in understanding.
It wasn't just her who was facing this problem, the rest of the Progenitors were the same.
Yes, they were all Transcendent Level beings, but they had no Laws. They were Pseudo Transcendents with no actual powers.
The Laws they had formed right now contained all their life experiences, but those very Laws themselves were no different than an Early Sovereign's Law.

Usually, at the Sovereign Stage, a cultivator understands the Law he has formed and refines it even further. As their understanding of their Law becomes stronger, they grow and break through to the Primordial Stage.
The Progenitors, however, had skipped that thought.
This had destabilized their foundation, and it already had a few permanent effects on their potential, but not everything was over.

These beings were still Pseudo Transcendents once, the Laws they had formed were strong already, not to mention Nux had turned all their Laws into Absolute, so while it was a pity that they couldn't unlock their complete potential to its fullest extent, if they focused on their foundation from now on, they could still become a force that couldn't be ignored.
"Thank you for your help."
Suddenly, Nux heard another voice.
It was Lilith, the Succubi Progenitor.
Nux turned towards her and smiled.

Too many things had happened between him and the Succubi Progenitor, the way she tried to change his mind, then the mess up inside the Illusion. Honestly, now that Nux looked back at it, it all turned out good.
After all, it was the Illusion that made it possible for him to create another Universe inside him.

The Illusion showed him that he couldn't form a Law because his Soul Father had already bound a Law to him. All he needed to do was to break through and he would have gotten a Law of his own. Of course, he didn't know that and continued to try and form a Law with a body that was incapable of forming a Law.
And because of those endless tries and constant pushes...
He formed something... even bigger than a Law.
Looking at it in a certain way, the very reason he was here was because of Lilith, which Nux appreciated. His wives, however, weren't the same.
They collectively disliked her and stayed away from her.
"It has been a while."
Nux greeted the woman.
Lilith hesitated.

Nux raised his eyebrow in surprise. To think the Succubi Queen of all people would hesitate. He wanted to stop her and tell her everything was alright, however, Faustina grabbed his hand, stopping him.
'Let her do it.
She has been thinking about it for a long time now.'
Nux nodded in understanding.
He stared at Lilith, giving her all the time she needed.
Lilith looked into his eyes and after a minute-long pause,
"I wanted to say this for a long time."
She started.
"I... I apologize for what I did back then. I used your wives to trick you into living in an illusionary world where you nearly lost your mind just so I could prove that I was right.
I was petty and small. I didn't think it through and arrogantly believed I was right till the end.
I apologize."
The Progenitor bowed her head, or she tried to. Nux, however, waved his hand and used Absolute Kinesis to stop her from doing that.
"It doesn't matter what you did."
He smiled.
Then, he glanced at the woman's guilty expression, and a playful smile appeared on his face,
"After all, in the end, I proved you were wrong.
I won~"
Lilith's mouth twitched at those words.
But for some reason...
These words eased her heart much more than anything she had imagined.
"I told you I would win, didn't I?
How does it feel to lose? Hmmmmm??"
"You are lucky that you are stronger than me, you brat."
Lilith snorted.
"Just you wait."
She threatened.
"Heh, like you can surpass me."
A vein popped on Lilith's forehead.
Those words hurt even more because she knew it was the truth.
"Fuck you, you brat!!"
"You wish~"
"Aaaaaaaahhhhhh!!!"
Lilith shouted as she tried to grab Nux's neck, ready to kill this shameless bastard.
Nux, of course, teleported away, but he made sure not to get too far. He still wanted Lilith to chase after him.
After all, what sane man would not want a beautiful woman chasing after him?
"Nux Leander! I will kill you!!"
As for how she was chasing after him to kill him...
Now that was just a minor detail, wasn't it?
Nux laughed at that thought as he ran, making the Succubus chase after him.
"You seem to be having fun."
Then suddenly, everyone present heard a voice. A voice that the Progenitors did not recognize, but Nux did.
"Did you like my gift?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1947 I will never harm you.
paragraphs: "You seem to be having fun.
Did you like my gift?"
Suddenly, everyone heard a playful voice, but before they could react, their movements slowed down.
Everyone but Nux moved unbearably slowly; they were almost frozen.
Nux, who noticed the odd change, turned around, and his eyes fell on a woman he knew very well.
She was here.
"The Seer."
He called out as he narrowed his eyes.
Right now, his thoughts on the Seer were complex.
He had doubted her before; he had even racked his brains trying to come up with ways to kill the woman, but let alone killing her, even tracking her down seemed impossible.
Yet now...
She was standing right in front of him with that same playful smile on her face.
"It doesn't look like you liked my gift very much.
Why is that?"
The woman questioned as she tilted her head in a curious frown.
"You should know that already, don't you? After all, you are the all-knowing Seer."
Nux retorted in a sarcastic tone.
"I do know the reason; I just do not understand why you still hold your grudges."
The Seer answered.
"I am sure you have finally realized what I did was necessary. I gave you a way out, a way to sever all your wives' connections with the Universe and be inseparable.
Is that not what you wanted?"
"You made my wife cry."
"I don't see her crying right now. She looks rather happy."
The Seer spoke as she glanced at Aeliana, who was still smiling and looking in Nux's direction.
In the end, Nux turned silent.

Even he could see that his anger towards the Seer was more of frustration, pettiness even. He had been in control for such a long time that now that a variable he couldn't control had appeared, he felt... strange.
"I know you do not trust me, Nux. I also know you were planning to track me down and kill me.
But I am not an enemy, Nux Leander.
Azriel Ruinous needed a push, and I gave it to him."
"You told him he would die."

"I only did it because I knew how he would react to my words. If I had directly told him to break his connection with Yrniel and kill himself, even if it was something he had thought of on his own, he would have doubted that I was scheming something and wanted him gone.
Of course, you being suspicious of me from the very start didn't help the situation either. That would have made him doubt me even more.
The only way out of this was to stroke his ego, tell him he couldn't do it, and see what happened next."
The Seer explained, and in the end, Nux turned silent.
After all, this was exactly how it had played out.
"Nux, I know you are doubtful, and truthfully, I wanted you to doubt me because I wanted Azriel to doubt me.
But now that is over, it is time I make something clear.
No matter what happens,
I will never harm you."
The woman spoke, her tone displaying affection and possessiveness very similar to his own.
It was almost too believable.
"Yes, I know it is hard for you, but you cannot deny I made things easier for you.
Even if you cannot see me as someone you can blindly trust, at the very least, you can see me as an ally. An ally who has a common enemy."
"Common enemy?"
"The Supreme Worlds."
The Seer revealed.
"But you said the Supreme Worlds cannot hurt you."
"That doesn't mean I can harm them. I already mentioned this before—I am not as strong as you may think. I am just complex to understand."
"So... you want me to help you fight the Supreme Worlds?"
"If that means you will stop looking at me like I am an enemy, then yes.
That gaze hurts, you know?
And I am saying this right now—I will make you pay for looking at me like that in the future."
Nux stayed silent.
"Your father-in-law is currently the Supreme Worlds' greatest enemy, the biggest thorn in their eyes."
The Seer mentioned out of the blue.
"Those Four will not sit back and let someone else surpass them all. They will come for Azriel."
"Why are you telling me that?"
Nux frowned.
"I am telling you because I want you to know that I am not the only one who sees the Supreme Worlds as enemies. Since your father-in-law will stand against them, they will be your enemies as well.
So stop thinking we do not have a common enemy."
"I was not..."
Nux tried to lie, but in the end, he just gave up.
He couldn't deal with this woman.
It was as if she knew everything he had in his mind.
Not to mention she was too beautiful.
It was a deadly combination.
In the end, Nux shook his head and heaved a big sigh.
"So you are an ally, got it."
"Good."
A beautiful smile appeared on the Seer's face.

Nux questioned.

The Seer questioned with a playful smile on her face.
"Don't you already know what I mean?"
Nux raised his eyebrow.

Her voice became low. Soon, however, she shook her head, as if getting rid of an unnecessary memory, and glanced at Nux again.
"So? What do you mean?"
She questioned.
Nux stared at the woman for a while. He still had many questions in his mind, but in the end, he decided to bury them all and trust her a little.

I may have become a Primordial now, but I am nowhere near strong enough to take on an Infinity-Level Being.
So how do we deal with the Supreme Worlds coming after us?"

sentences.text: "You seem to be having fun.
Did you like my gift?"
Suddenly, everyone heard a playful voice, but before they could react, their movements slowed down.
Everyone but Nux moved unbearably slowly; they were almost frozen.
Nux, who noticed the odd change, turned around, and his eyes fell on a woman he knew very well.
She was here.
"The Seer."
He called out as he narrowed his eyes.
Right now, his thoughts on the Seer were complex.
He had doubted her before; he had even racked his brains trying to come up with ways to kill the woman, but let alone killing her, even tracking her down seemed impossible.
Yet now...
She was standing right in front of him with that same playful smile on her face.
"It doesn't look like you liked my gift very much.
Why is that?"
The woman questioned as she tilted her head in a curious frown.
"You should know that already, don't you?
After all, you are the all-knowing Seer."
Nux retorted in a sarcastic tone.
"I do know the reason; I just do not understand why you still hold your grudges."
The Seer answered.
"I am sure you have finally realized what I did was necessary.
I gave you a way out, a way to sever all your wives' connections with the Universe and be inseparable.
Is that not what you wanted?"
"You made my wife cry."
"I don't see her crying right now.
She looks rather happy."
The Seer spoke as she glanced at Aeliana, who was still smiling and looking in Nux's direction.
In the end, Nux turned silent.
Even he could see that his anger towards the Seer was more of frustration, pettiness even.
He had been in control for such a long time that now that a variable he couldn't control had appeared, he felt... strange.
"I know you do not trust me, Nux.
I also know you were planning to track me down and kill me.
But I am not an enemy, Nux Leander.
Azriel Ruinous needed a push, and I gave it to him."
"You told him he would die."
"I only did it because I knew how he would react to my words.

If I had directly told him to break his connection with Yrniel and kill himself, even if it was something he had thought of on his own, he would have doubted that I was scheming something and wanted him gone.
Of course, you being suspicious of me from the very start didn't help the situation either.
That would have made him doubt me even more.
The only way out of this was to stroke his ego, tell him he couldn't do it, and see what happened next."
The Seer explained, and in the end, Nux turned silent.

chapters.title: Chapter 1948 Why Azriel?
paragraphs: "How do we deal with the Supreme Worlds coming after us?"
Nux questioned directly, doing exactly what the Seer told him to do. The woman smiled. She knew Nux still had doubts, but she appreciated his actions.
Their relationship was finally blossoming.
For an instant, she lost herself in her own fantasies. Soon, however, she shook her head and answered Nux's question.
"You do not have to worry about that.
Those fools are currently busy fighting amongst themselves, trying to find out who amongst them is the Universe's Child and come up with ways to end his existence."
"So they do not know who the Universe's Child actually is?"
"Of course not. If they did, Azriel would have died. You think the Universe would make it so easy to kill its Child?
They just know the Universe has chosen a Child, and they believe it is one of them because who else would it be?
After all, they are the entities closest to the Universe—or at least, that is what they believe."
The Seer spoke sarcastically. Clearly, she wasn't fond of the Four Supreme Worlds.
"What does 'entities closest to the Universe' mean? Actually, was there a reason the Universe chose Lord Azriel as its Child? If yes, then do you know what it is?"
Nux asked a series of questions.
The Seer momentarily turned silent, making Nux frown.
"What? Is it something I will not understand again?"
"You see..."
The Seer smiled wryly.
However, just as Nux was about to sigh in disappointment, the woman gave in, unable to see that look on his face.
"Alright, I'll try to explain.
Think of it this way: if the Universe's strength is 100, then Infinities are at 60, the Eternals are at 8, Transcendents 1, and others don't matter."
"That's quite a big gap between Eternals and Infinities."
Nux commented.
"It is accurate."
The Seer nodded, once again returning to the main topic.

"According to this scale, Infinities are obviously closest to the Universe, and while this scale may represent strength, it also represents the connection between the Universe and an entity inside it.
After all, the essence of cultivation is understanding your Law, and as you understand your Law, you get closer to the Universe.
So the living entities closest to the Universe are indeed Infinities. The more powerful their Law and the better their understanding of it, the closer they are.
In our scale, this could be like the Infinities from Supreme Level Worlds being somewhere around 60, while Azriel is at 61."
"So the reason Azriel was chosen was because he was the strongest?"
"Yes, that is one way to look at it. Strength isn't exactly the only factor either.
Azriel is also trustworthy and has a track record."
"A track record?"
Nux frowned.
"Yrniel."
The Seer answered.
"Azriel protected Yrniel when it was on the verge of destruction."
"Doesn't every Progenitor protect his own world?"
"Azriel is different. He protected Yrniel from threats that should have destroyed it."
"But Yrniel was..."
Nux frowned, not knowing if he should say it or not.
The Seer, however, shook her head.
"Yes, it was the Incarnation of the Supreme World, so you think no other world other than Supreme Worlds should be threats that should have destroyed it.
But that is wrong.
When Azriel was born, Yrniel was already reduced to a Low-Level World.

Creating two long-lasting shields, extending the Progenitors' lives, and creating so many Progenitors in the first place already took away most of its energy. Even a Middle-Level World should have been more than enough to destroy it.
But then,
Azriel was born, and in a world where one could only reach the Primordial Level, he formed a Law so strong that it gave Yrniel hope.
Yrniel, using whatever energy it had, supported him, allowing him to break his limits, and he didn't disappoint.
He got stronger and stronger and reached a point where no one in the entire Universe could stand up to him.
Azriel was... Yrniel's Hero.
And now, he is the Universe's Hero."
"So this is why the Universe chose him over other Infinities..."
"Mhm, those at the Supreme Worlds never had a chance. The Universe was always going to choose Azriel—I just pushed it a little to make that choice faster."
"Hmm? What?"
Nux frowned.
"You pushed the Universe to make that choice faster?"
"Mhm."
The Seer nodded.
"The Universe would have chosen Azriel, yes.
The Anomaly had only targeted a few beings and entities; it hadn't taken something the Universe actually cherished.
The Universe was angry, not desperate.
However, Azriel's act of risking his own life for the chance of becoming stronger attracted the Universe's attention.
The strength to not give up even when you have no way out—it was a quality of a Hero.
A quality that impressed the Universe, and it finally decided.
It wanted Azriel by its side. Even if it still wasn't desperate, it wanted to see what Azriel would grow into.
So the Universe made a decision and connected its fate to the Hero's, just like Yrniel once did."
The Seer revealed the entire story, and Nux just stared at her with a surprised look on his face.
Once again, he couldn't help but be impressed by his father-in-law.
Soon, however, another question popped up in his mind.
"How long would it take for the Supreme Worlds to realize that the Universe's Chosen isn't amongst them?"
"I cannot tell you that."
"Why is that?"
"I have several restrictions. As much as I want to help you, I cannot do so because I know it would bring you more harm than good.
For now, the only thing I can tell you is to follow the same path you had planned and get stronger.
I believe now that you have nothing holding you back, you can move much more efficiently."
Nux nodded at those words, and the Seer smiled brightly.
"Gather all the Primordial Energies, Nux Leander.
Make your Universe self-reliant like you planned to, and
Get stronger."

chapters.title: Chapter 1949 A-Alright, I might be a little arrogant.
paragraphs: "So you want me to gather all the Primordial Energies, create life within my Universe, and let that life grow so once they break through the Divine Stage, I get stronger?"
"I do not want you to do that; it is what you had planned from the beginning."
"Right, you cannot interfere."
Nux nodded, and the Seer just smiled.
"What other Primordial Energies are there again?"
Nux questioned.
Of course, he knew he wouldn't be getting an answer. He just needed someone who could listen to him and maybe try to get an answer from her expression.
"I already have the Primordial Energy of Creation, Death, Space, Destruction, and Life.
So how many are left?"
Nux asked, and once again, the Seer just smiled, not saying anything.
"Time?"
Nux questioned.
"You do realize that I know what you are trying to do, don't you?"
The Seer questioned with a playful smile.
"Come on, give me something."
"The number of times I can help you is limited. I do not want to waste it on something you already know."
"...so what you are saying is that the answer I have in my mind is correct?"
"I just know you have seen Life Form more than once.
So you should know the answer to that question."
The woman answered, and Nux instantly remembered the vision he saw every time he devoured a world.
A world created out of nothing but a combination of different Primordial Energies, out of which he recognized a few of them.
The Forces of Creation, Death, Space, Destruction, and Life—the energies he had comprehended, he could understand.
As for the energies he hadn't...
They were just... there.
Playing their role from its birth to destruction.
Nux remembered how these energies got stronger during a particular 'phase' of the world.
Like the Energy of Destruction and Death getting stronger during wars or natural calamities.
The Energy of Life, when the world was being populated, a peaceful era.
The Energy of Creation when the world was being created.
And the Energy of Space, to keep everything together.
All the energies acted like they were meant to, just like the other unknown energies that Nux failed to recognize.
An energy that was interwoven together with the Energy of Space all the time.
Energy that slightly strengthened during the day and the peaceful era.
Energy that strengthened during the night or when the times were grim.

Another energy that weakened every time the previous two energies got too strong, and the complete opposite of this energy—an energy that strengthened every time one of those two energies was strengthened, no matter which.
Obviously, Nux had a rough guess as to what these unknown energies were.
The energy interwoven with the Energy of Space was Time.
The energy that strengthened during the day and peace was Light.
The energy of grim times was Darkness.
The energy that balanced these two was Balance.
And the energy opposite to it was... Chaos.
Nux knew that... just that...
He wasn't sure about it.
But if the Seer was now telling him that he already knew the answer, it meant that what he was thinking was correct.
The other five energies that he needed to create an independent Universe.
"I know where I would get Light, Darkness, and Balance."
Nux muttered.
The Seer, however, shook her head, her tone strict.
"Did you forget what I told you? You are not strong enough to go near the Supreme Worlds. You go near them, and things will go wrong.
You cannot make a mistake here. You do not have Azriel protecting you any longer."
"I thought you weren't going to help me."
"I am only telling you what you already know.
I am helping you think, something I shouldn't be doing considering your mind is far more capable than most."
"But I do not know anything about Time and Chaos. I thought comprehending Vulpiana's Law would give me an insight into Time, but that didn't happen.
Even her Law was too weak.
The only other person I can think of is..."
Nux turned silent, looking at the Seer.
Obviously, both of them knew what he was talking about.
"What about the last one?"
The Seer questioned.
It was a clear attempt to change the topic, and Nux understood that.
He stared at the woman for a while, thinking.
He wasn't angry or frustrated.
Honestly, the Seer had helped him more than enough. Just solving Yrniel's trouble was quite a lot.
The woman, using her powers, protected Yrniel from any threats whatsoever.
She also gave a new life to his imprisoned father-in-law.
She had done more than enough.
Nux...
Nux trusted her.
Even if his instincts told him otherwise.
"I apologize."
Honestly, even Nux realized he was relying on her a little too much. Even if she hadn't appeared, he would need to comprehend other Primordial Energies on his own, without her help.
He shouldn't be asking her, and the Seer was trying to prevent that as well.
He couldn't cut his journey short, else... the Seer wouldn't see the Nux she wished to see.
"I apologize."
Nux spoke up.
The Seer smiled at him.
"Why apologize?"
She questioned.
Nux stared at her with a deadpan look on his face. Soon, however, he realized what she was trying to do.
"Alright, a normal conversation."
He nodded to himself and then,
"I apologize for doubting you. You helped me, and I was doubting you the entire time. I was even trying to come up with ways to get rid of you."
"How cruel~"
The Seer chuckled, and Nux just bowed his head.
"Did you come up with something?"
"I didn't."
Nux laughed as he scratched the back of his head. The Seer chuckled together with him.
"I didn't think you would admit it."
"You didn't?"
Nux raised his eyebrows.
"Well, considering how arrogant you are, any normal person would not think that."
"Hey, I am not that arrogant."
The silence was deafening.
Nux couldn't see the woman's eyes, but he could feel it.
Her stare, her looking right into his eyes, telling him to self-reflect...
And for some reason, her reaction affected him.
"A-Alright, I might be a little arrogant."
He admitted his defeat.

Nux couldn't see the woman's eyes, but he could feel it.
Her stare, her looking right into his eyes, telling him to self-reflect...
And for some reason, her reaction affected him.
"A-Alright, I might be a little arrogant."
He admitted his defeat.

chapters.title: Chapter 1950 Bloodedge.
paragraphs: "A-Alright, I might be a little arrogant."
Nux folded.
For some reason, the woman had more effect on him than he would like to admit.
"I didn't think you would admit this either."
The Seer chuckled again, and this time,
"Oh, come on!"
Nux just complained.
"I may be arrogant, but I am reasonable with my allies. If you were an enemy, I would have done anything in my power to try and kill you, if not today, then tomorrow perhaps.
But since you are an ally, I am not ashamed to admit that I cannot defeat you in any way. I am helpless...
For now."
"See? This is the arrogant self I am talking about."
The Seer chuckled and...
'Fuck, I am arrogant.'
Nux had a new realization.
"Alright, alright."
He then shook his head, not wanting to get distracted anymore.
"As I said, I apologize for doubting you before and... also for not saying this earlier."
Nux then stared at the Seer and with an earnest look on his face,
"Thank you."
He expressed his gratitude.
"I thought you were going to confess."
The Seer chuckled.
"Do you want me to?"
Nux questioned back with a smile.

"What kind of man asks that question? You should be more confident in yourself and do what your heart desires. Asking a woman if they want to get a confession before actually confessing shows self-doubt."
The Seer gave a lecture with a genuine smile on her face,
As if she was enjoying their conversation.
"Well, you were the one who brought up confession, so it isn't my fault."
"This is the moment where you usually confess."
The Seer answered, slightly disappointed, but Nux just smiled.
"You should already know wh-"
However, before he could say anything, the woman placed a finger on his lips, forcing him to stop.
"I do not know anything."
She repeated herself, this time, her tone heavier than before, as if she didn't want Nux to forget about it.
"Heh."
Nux laughed at that.
Then, he closed his eyes and sighed.
"If it was a normal scenario, I would have indeed confessed. I would have talked about how I was going to chase you to the end of the universe and wouldn't let you go, but..."
Nux paused for a moment as he stared at the woman again,
"I have this feeling that... you won't be staying with me right now."
The Seer smiled at those words.
"I cannot stay with you right now."
She answered honestly.
"The change will be too big, I cannot afford that.
I might already be ruining things by staying here longer than I intended to, but...
I can't seem to leave."
The woman spoke with a weak smile on her face.
"Maybe my heart desires a few more minutes."
She chuckled. Nux, however, could sense the very slight trembling in her voice.
He gulped, feeling a lump forming in his throat. He, however, controlled his emotions and,
"I cannot stay away from the people I love. I need them next to me, all the time."
"I understand."
The Seer nodded.
"Alright, let us stop this and return to what actually matters."
"What actually matters?"
Nux frowned for a moment.
"I took away your weapon, remember?"
The Seer questioned.
"You did."
"Here."
Nux's breathing hitched for a moment as his eyes fell on a sword with an obsidian blade with veins of crimson that pulsed like living fire, radiating both power and something ancient and... ominous.
*Image*
The instant that sword appeared in front of him, Nux couldn't look away. It was as if the sword had hypnotized him to not look away.
He couldn't even look at the Seer's face and,
"What is it?"
He questioned.
"I took a sword from you. It is only right that I give you something in return, isn't it?"
The Seer smiled as she presented the sword, and unable to control himself, Nux quickly grabbed the hilt.
And the instant he did, his body trembled as he felt a strange, creepy energy that he couldn't understand crawling all over his body, ready to chew away his body.
When the Seer noticed his reaction, she smiled.
"Bloodedge."
She said.
"That's her name."
"She is a Relic, Nux."
"A Relic?"
Nux frowned.
He obviously knew what a Relic was, and he was sure he would recognize a relic if he saw one... but this...
This sword didn't look like a Relic...
As if knowing what he was thinking, the Seer chuckled.
"She is different from what you people call Relics. She is a True Relic.
Well, to put it in terms you would understand, this is what you can call a Supreme Level Relic.
A Relic capable of cutting anything or anyone, no matter the level."
"No matter the level...?"
Nux raised his brows at those words, and the Seer nodded.
"Yes, even Eternals and Infinites."
"What...?"
Nux couldn't believe what he was hearing.
"You are telling me I can kill Infinities with this...?"
"You should know it better than I do, Nux.
You cannot even defeat an Eternal right now."
The Seer shook her head.
"I am merely stating that if you can swing her at them and your attack somehow connects, this sword will not fail you.
You will cut them, even kill them if you cut in the right place, but..."
"As I am right now, I cannot even get close to them."
Nux knew his limits, and the Seer nodded.
"She is the perfect weapon I have chosen for you. A weapon that will not fail you no matter how strong you become.
I also made sure she is her instead of a him to suit you well."
The Seer chuckled.
"A her, huh..."
Nux laughed as well.
"Right, she does suck a lot of energy, even when she is not being used and is inside your storage ring, but that's not a problem, is it?"
"It is not."
Nux chuckled.
"Then link with it."
Seer ordered and before Nux did it, he looked at the woman one last time and she nodded.
"Yes, Eternity won't know, don't worry.
She is the Second of the Three Gifts I have prepared for you."
